Two days after devastating floods caused by a glacier collapse along the Nepal-Tibet border, authorities are monitoring dangerous barrier lakes on both sides. On Nepal's side, a debris dam broke its banks, causing the Bhote Koshi river to rise and temporarily halting rescue flights. Across the border in China, a lake near Gyirong holding over 2.5 million cubic metres of water posed a high breach risk, though authorities said it was draining naturally. The disaster began when a massive section of glacier ice and rock collapsed into the Lhende Khola river system, creating a natural dam that eventually gave way, sending a powerful surge of water, mud and rock downstream, destroying roads, bridges, and settlements. #nepal #tibet #flood

This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. It’s already 2083 in Nepal 🇳🇵📅 Nepal’s official calendar, Bikram Sambat, runs almost 57 years ahead, and New Year lands in April. Even stranger: its months can be anywhere from 29 to 32 days long, and the lengths change every year because they follow the sun’s real path across the sky. No simple formula, so you need the new official calendar just to know how long the months are. What year would you rather live in?  #Nepal #Calendar #History #FunFacts #NepaliNewYear

Your odds of being born in Nepal are about 1 in 240: roughly 552,000 babies a year out of about 132 million born worldwide. Nepal has the only national flag in the world that isn't a rectangle. Its official calendar, Bikram Sambat, is already in the year 2083. The country runs on UTC+5:45, fifteen minutes ahead of India. Eight of the world's ten highest mountains are in Nepal, including Everest. Nepal was never colonised by a European power. And in Kathmandu, a young girl is worshipped as a living goddess: the Kumari. November 14, 2026 Gorkha District, Nepal A large dry landslide occurred in Gorkha District. A mass of earth and rock collapsed from the Gundrung Pakha slope into the Thado Bharyang forest area near Yarubagar. Rocks began falling as early as Friday night, and the main landslide took place around 8:30 a.m., kicking up a massive cloud of dust. Debris reached the Budhi Gandaki River. The landslide blocked both a motorable road and a foot trail. According to the district police, there were no casualties or material damage.
